jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Sustainable Indoor Solar Cells for Ambient Light Energy Harvesting in IoT Applications - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing thin-film solar cells designed to operate efficiently under indoor lighting and thereby contributing to the green transition? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to break new ground by harvesting energy from ambient light and help pave the way towards sustainable technologies.

The Thin-Film Photovoltaics Group at DTU Electro is seeking candidates for a PhD Scholarship focused on the development and characterization of highly efficient Sb₂S₃ solar cells. You will investigate materials, interfaces, and device architectures to understand and overcome the fundamental limitations of photovoltaic performance under low-light conditions.

The position is offered within the framework of DTU’s Alliances and Strategic Partnerships with Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Estonia. You will be part of an international research collaboration combining thin-film synthesis, solar-cell fabrication, advanced optoelectronic and defect characterization, and device testing under realistic illumination conditions. As part of the PhD project, you will undertake a research stay at TalTech and work closely with researchers from both universities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project focuses on developing high-efficiency Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells for indoor energy harvesting. The project will investigate how material properties, interfaces, and device architecture influence charge transport, recombination, and voltage losses under low-intensity illumination. The overall objective is to develop solar cells optimized for indoor light and demonstrate series-connected mini-modules capable of powering battery-free IoT devices.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Develop and optimize Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells by engineering device architectures and interfaces to enhance charge collection while minimizing recombination and voltage losses under indoor illumination.
• Characterize solar cells under different LED spectra, light intensities, and illumination conditions relevant to realistic indoor environments.
• Investigate defect states, interface recombination, and open-circuit voltage losses, including advanced electrical characterization during a research stay at TalTech.
• Develop and characterize series-connected indoor photovoltaic mini-modules for battery-free IoT applications.
• Supervise and contribute to MSc/BSc student projects.
• Document and disseminate the research through scientific publications and international conference contributions
You should have a strong academic background in physics, chemistry, materials science, nanotechnology, or a related field. Prior knowledge of semiconductor physics and photovoltaics, and experience with thin-film materials, solar-cell fabrication, optoelectronic characterization, or indoor photovoltaics, would be particularly valuable.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be made by Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms. 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is the 1 February 2027. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from the Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu, email stec@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
A three-year position as a Postdoctoral researcher is now available at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The Postdoc’s employment is expected to start on 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  About the Center

  You will be employed at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, which aims to build a strong scientific foundation for understanding and acting on complex public-health challenges. The Center leverages multi-layered nationwide social and health data combined with an interdisciplinary fusion of methods spanning data science, epidemiology, ethnography, econometrics, and systems science. Our research focuses on the complex interplay of health, social, and environmental factors that shape individuals, families, and networks over time. We emphasise interdisciplinary collaboration, offering you an opportunity to actively engage as a collaborative partner in different projects depending on your interests and expertise. Learn more about the Center and our research, vision, and values here.

  About the Department 

  The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

  About the position 

  The position will be nested within the Child Health group at the Center, where we advance knowledge through a combination of research activities that leverage the Center’s data infrastructures and methodological expertise, and engagement with policymakers and practitioners. The Center has developed a strategic partnership with a Danish municipality – the Thriving Communities Lab – which offers a platform for connecting the scientific activities at the Center with real-world health promotion efforts. The focus of this partnership is to enhance the conditions for adolescents to thrive through a dynamic learning process that involves professionals across sectors in the municipality, the local government, and researchers, over a period of several years. One question we will explore is whether computational modelling can usefully bring together local knowledge, scientific evidence, the Center’s data resources, and insights emerging from practical interventions, and so strengthen this learning process. Your work as a postdoc will be anchored around this question. Our vision at the Center is to build on this experience to engage with more municipalities over time, addressing a variety of complex health challenges.

  As a Postdoc, your responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• Spearheading the development of a decision-support/scenario exploration tool that offers policymakers a way to visualize and simulate systemic effects of social investments and programmes, in close collaboration with our partners in the Thriving Communities Lab. 	
• Engaging with municipal collaborators within the Thriving Communities Lab to ensure a dynamic interplay between research activities and local efforts. 	
• Exploring multi-layered life-course data from the Danish Life Course Cohort (DANLIFE), augmented with local data from the municipal partner, to map the interrelated landscape of well-being among adolescents. 	
• Contributing to scientific publications and engage in the dissemination of research results related to these topics. 	
• Collaborating with researchers in the Center on interdisciplinary projects. 	
• Participating in research-based teaching at the Department of Public Health. 	
• Actively contributing to the development of organisational elements within the Center, such as network activities, website, outreach initiatives, social engagements, scientific meetings, and more.   Profile 

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with the following competences and experience:

   	
• You have a PhD degree in social science, economics, epidemiology, data science, complexity science, computational science, or other related sciences. 	
• You have experience with system dynamics modelling. Experience with agent-based modelling, social return on investment analysis or other analytical frameworks to model social and systemic impacts of social policies and programmes would also be an advantage. 	
• Experience working with Danish register data is an advantage. 	
• You are motivated to engage in participatory processes with practitioners and policymakers, and to collaborate with a variety of stakeholders to foster change. 	
• You have an active interest in complex-systems science applied to public health and epidemiology. 	
• You have proficient communication skills and a proven ability to work in interdisciplinary teams. 	
• You have excellent English skills, both written and spoken. 	
• Danish language skills are an advantage but not essential.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, next to the Lakes in Central Copenhagen.

  Terms of employment 
 The average working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is February 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark for the past 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Further information

  For specific information about the position, please contact the Associate professor Christopher Jamil de Montgomery: cmon@sund.ku.dk

  Applicants may find the following links useful:

   	
• Copenhagen Health Complexity Center: https://healthcomplex.dk/ 	
• University of Copenhagen: http://ku.dk/english/ 	
• Department of Public Health: http://publichealth.ku.dk/ 	
• International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/   Application process

  Your application should be written in English and must include the following documents – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter of motivation (max 1 page). Please briefly describe your previous research experience and interests as well as what attracts you to the position. 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 	
• Certified/signed copies of
 	a) PhD certificate (if the PhD has not been completed, a written statement from the applicant’s supervisor will suffice)
 	b) Master of Science certificate. 	
• A research plan (max 2 pages) outlining your ideas for how a decision-support/scenario exploration tool could be developed, drawing on system dynamics modelling or other analytical frameworks suitable for modelling dynamic effects of social policies and programmes.   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be considered.

  After the expiration of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been advanced for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each applicant is given an opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves.

  You can read more about the recruitment process here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Application deadline 

  Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 47-48.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

You will build and run its engine keeping the Product and Marketing finance team connected to the financial heartbeat of the company: one planning calendar, one reporting standard, cost control across worldwide envelopes, and an automation toolchain that makes reporting produce itself. You are shaping how this team runs, and the role grows as the toolchain does. As we build the team capabilities, we continue delivering results every quarter, budget every autumn, and the value optimization discipline that funds our growth.

This is a role for someone who is a pace setter, taking real pride in a rhythm that builds credibility, and who wants to modernize how the work gets done.

What you will do

• Own the Product and Marketing financial planning calendar end to end: budget and long-range planning milestones, forecast cycles, month-end and performance review inputs, orchestrating and collaborating so that every corporate deadline is met reliably and consistently.

• Own the reporting catalogue with clear service levels, and build the automation toolchain that produces the recurring suite, retiring manual production as you go.

• Run the functional line into our Global Business Services team: process catalogue, quality, capacity, one blueprint.

• Run cost control for the CMO, CPO and Global Office envelopes as a trusted, independent service.

• Front the team's interface to FP&A and the CFO office, reconciling to one set of definitions.

What is needed to succeed

• 7-10 years in financial planning, reporting or control; you have run a planning calendar or close process end to end.

• Experience building or running a shared-services or offshore interface, with the catalogue and quality rhythm to show for it.

• At least one recurring reporting process you automated, with the manual version retired, and genuine energy for doing it again at scale.

• The independence to hold deadlines, definitions and spend hygiene, including with colleagues more senior than you.

Who you are

• A self-starter: you see the missing process and build it before anyone asks.

• You develop and defend your own point of view: the calendar and the definitions are yours, and you can say no and make it stick, respectfully.

• You believe finance is a strategic copilot to the business, and control done well, an essential guardrail to earn investors' and consumers' trust.

• You can have difficult conversations respectfully, and colleagues trust you more because of them.

• Consumer-centric at heart: you keep the numbers connected to the people who wear the jewellery.

• People-first and collaborator: you make a shared-services team feel like one team, across sites and time zones.

Reporting into the Sr Director, Global Product & Marketing Finance, you will be the backbone of a small, senior team with a mandate from the top of the company, and you contribute by making excellent work systematic.

Additional information

Global Career Band 4B - Manager.

Hybrid Working Flexibility – 3 days in office per week

Location Copenhagen; Global scope.

English is our working language; Danish is not required.

Did we get your attention?

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

At Pandora, we believe that creating an inclusive and diverse workplace and reflecting societal diversity in our customer engagement is essential to delivering on our company purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We dedicate ourselves to fostering, cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and diversity where everyone feels respected and valued.

jobs.description:
Are you an accomplished enterprise sales leader ready to shape the future of cyber defence? Join a world-class team helping organizations protect their operations while building Deloitte’s Managed Security Services business across the Nordics. If you have created enterprise pipelines, closed complex deals and thrived in high-growth environments, this could be your next move.

We are looking for a Sales Director / Senior Sales Executive to join our fast-growing Nordic Cyber team and lead sales for our Managed Security Services offering.

About us

Deloitte is recognized as the world’s leading trusted cybersecurity advisor. We help complex organizations pursue their growth, innovation, and performance agendas with greater confidence by proactively managing cyber risk. By combining advisory, implementation, and managed services, we help clients transform cyber risks into a competitive advantage.

Our globally recognized Managed Security Services practice helps clients understand who may attack them and why, then build the detection and response capabilities needed to stay ahead of threats. We help organizations prepare for cyber incidents, respond to and recover from crises, and resume operations more quickly while limiting business impact. Across 150+ countries, we protect more than 10,000 enterprise clients through 24/7 Security Operations Centers and industry-leading threat detection and response capabilities.

You can read more about our services within Cyber team at Deloitte here

Your role

The Managed Security Services (MSS) market is experiencing explosive growth—projected at 12-15% CAGR through 2028. As a Sales Director at Deloitte, you’ll own a multi-million-dollar sales pipeline, lead complex enterprise deals, and shape the future of how organizations defend against evolving cyber threats.

This is NOT just a transactional sales role. This is a strategic sales leadership position where you’ll:

• 
Own full responsibility for MSS sales in the Nordics

• 
Partner with C-suite executives to position cybersecurity as a business risk management imperative

• 
Work with most innovative and security-conscious growth and Fortune 500 organizations

• 
Influence product strategy and service innovation across a global practice

• 
Work internationally across Deloitte’s Cyber practice

As part of our Cyber team in this role, your main responsibility areas would be:

Strategic ownership

• 
Own the full sales lifecycle from pipeline creation through deal closure and account expansion

• 
Drive revenue growth, exploit the market opportunities

• 
Build and lead a sales team and develop the next generation of cyber sales leaders

• 
Shape go-to-market strategy for emerging MSS offerings and disruptive security trends

Enterprise Sales Leadership

• 
Qualify, shape, and close complex deals (€1M-€10M+) with C-suite decision-makers

• 
Position cybersecurity as business risk management, not a technical product—speaking the language of CISOs, CFOs, CROs, and CEOs

• 
Navigate 6-18 month sales cycles with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and complex procurement processes

• 
Develop strategic account plans for target enterprises and identifying expansion opportunities within existing clients

Collaboration & Innovation

• 
Partner with account and delivery leadership to ensure deal quality, innovative solutions, and client success

• 
Influence product and service strategy by bringing market intelligence, competitive insights, and client feedback

• 
Leverage Deloitte’s global network to access resources, thought leadership, productive relationships and cross-border opportunities

• 
Drive process improvement initiatives that strengthen Deloitte’s competitive positioning

Client Relationship Excellence

• 
Serve as trusted advisor to key accounts, understanding their business objectives and evolving threat landscape

• 
Build lasting relationships with security leaders, risk officers, and business executives

• 
Develop strategic partnerships with key accounts, positioning Deloitte as an indispensable partner in their cyber transformation journey

What do we offer?

🟢Deloitte employs 35,000+ cyber practitioners worldwide. We serve the biggest and most innovative companies across the globe as well as locally in the Nordics – solving complex problems, achieving remarkable goals, and making meaningful progress. We refer to ourselves as cyber leaders, strategists, advisors, hackers, and specialists. You would be selling to most innovative and security-conscious organizations while leveraging cutting-edge threat intelligence and AI assisted SOC capabilities as competitive differentiators

🟢Create your own growth and success path autonomously. This position with rapid MSS demand provides exceptional and accelerated growth opportunity as you are given an opportunity to build a team and scale a practice from the ground up with clear path to leadership and Partner level

🟢Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus structure/incentives and comprehensive benefits package

🟢In the Nordics, we are an empowered team, gearing for growth together in an entity where it has been done many times before. We want to offer our professionals as flexible working conditions as possible and thus, we work in a hybrid model. You are warmly welcome to our cozy office in Helsinki, Stockholm, Copenhagen or Oslo, but you can work flexibly and remotely as well

🟢You won’t be working alone — you will work alongside top-tier sales professionals, collaborate with our international multidisciplinary team of strategists, advisors and cyber professionals regarded as industry leaders who bring a balanced mix of technical, legal, and business expertise to support you.  Throughout your journey with us, you'll have access to Deloitte University and global professional development programs to continuously advance your skills, complemented by mentorship from senior partners and exposure to our global leadership network.

We look forward to receiving your application!

📩 Questions about the recruitment process: You can read more about us and our recruitment process on our website. If you did not find the answer you were looking for, please contact our recruitment team at rekry@deloitte.fi

At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, perspectives, and experiences, as they enable us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team’s success.

You will have the opportunity to work alongside over 450,000 colleagues globally and nearly 900 colleagues in Finland across Audit & Assurance, Tax & Legal, and Consulting services. At Deloitte, it’s all about people, each with something special to offer. We collaborate closely with one another and with our clients, making great things happen. That’s how we create real change.

Deloitte is where you’ll find unlimited opportunities to succeed and realise your full potential, together.

About the job

We are looking for an experienced IAM Tech Lead to provide technical leadership across our Identity & Access Management landscape and accelerate our journey towards a more automated, standardized and engineering-driven IAM environment.

You will help define the technical direction across Identity Governance & Administration, Directory Services, Authentication & Federation, Privileged Access Management, PKI and IAM Engineering & Automation, working closely with platform and service owners.

A key focus will be to reduce manual IAM operations through automation and standardization, using APIs, scripting, workflow orchestration, Infrastructure as Code and CI/CD.

Drive the technical implementation of the IAM Service Intake and Automation Model, standardizing and automating IAM requests across Jira, ServiceNow, IGA and other IAM platforms.

You will establish reusable engineering patterns for integrations, automation, testing, deployment and monitoring, while improving the resilience and operational readiness of IAM services.

As a hands-on technical leader, you will lead complex IAM designs and modernization initiatives, guide engineers and contribute directly to integrations, automation and troubleshooting.

Our IAM landscape includes Omada, Microsoft Active Directory and Entra ID, Ping Identity, Delinea PAM, HashiCorp Vault/Boundary and enterprise PKI.

What you will help drive:

IAM Technical Leadership

Provide technical direction across the IAM landscape, lead complex solution designs and establish common technical standards in collaboration with IAM platform and service owners.

IAM Engineering & Automation

Transform manual IAM processes into API-driven and automated services using scripting, workflow automation, Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD and automated testing.

Service Intake & Orchestration

Drive the technical implementation of standardized IAM service intake, routing, orchestration and automated fulfilment across Jira, ServiceNow, IGA and other IAM platforms.

IAM Modernization

Reduce legacy dependencies and technical debt while supporting the transition towards modern, scalable and resilient identity technologies.

Engineering Standards & Reliability

Establish reusable patterns for source control, integrations, configuration management, testing, deployment, monitoring and logging to ensure IAM automation is maintainable and operationally reliable.

"We are looking for someone who can combine deep IAM expertise with an engineering mindset and help us move from manual processes towards standardized and automated identity services. This is an opportunity to help shape how we engineer and modernize IAM across TDC NET," says Abhishek Kumar, Senior Manager, IAM, TDC NET

We are looking for someone who combines engineering and automation mindset and expertise within IAM area.

• 7+ years of professional experience within Identity & Access Management, including significant experience in senior engineering, solution design or technical leadership responsibilities

• Extensive experience with IAM engineering, solution design and enterprise integrations

• Direct experience with automation, APIs and scripting, using PowerShell, Python or similar technologies

• Experience with DevOps engineering practices, including Git, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, configuration management and automated testing

• Experience designing API-driven integrations, workflow orchestration and automated service fulfilment

• Deep knowledge of enterprise directory, identity and access technologies, including Active Directory, Entra ID, OpenLDAP, Keycloak or equivalent platforms, with solid understanding of identity lifecycle management, authentication, authorization and federation.

• Experience with key IAM capabilities such as IGA, SSO/Federation, MFA, PAM, PKI and Secrets Management

• Ability to define technical standards, reusable engineering patterns and implementation guardrails

• Ability to lead technical designs, troubleshoot complex problems and provide technical guidance to engineers

• Extensive understanding of security principles including Zero Trust, least privilege, privileged access and segregation of duties

You are comfortable moving between architecture, engineering and implementation. You can create technical direction while remaining close enough to the technology to build, challenge and troubleshooting solutions.

You naturally look at repetitive activities and ask how they can be standardized, automated and operated more efficiently.
